title: CINETRA: A Multi-Vendor Audit of Semantic Concept Transfer in Cardiac MRI (code, protocol and frozen results)

description:
CINETRA (cine semantic transition) audits what a frozen cardiac MRI classifier encodes, in the quantities a reader measures: ventricular volumes, ejection fractions and myocardial mass. A typed linear transition maps the classifier's 57 mask descriptors to measured concepts; variable-precision rough-set rules on the concepts must pass a cross-fitted gate before they may label a case; and every case receives one reason-coded route, a label or a computational abstention. The audit was registered as a signed protocol (CMR-TRANS-AUDIT 6.0.0 and its 6.0.1 amendment), frozen, and evaluated once on three public cohorts (ACDC, M&Ms-1 and M&Ms-2), one of them held out and unread until the registration.

This archive is the study's public record: the code that produced the results (byte-identical to the registered commits), the protocol with its signed amendments and a verifiable proof of their registration, the aggregate results of the frozen run, the evidence packs of the post-freeze exploratory analyses of amendments 6.0.2 and later (exploratory, post hoc), the objects fitted on the ACDC development set, the figures, and tools to verify the registration and the datasets and to compare a re-run with the frozen results. Apart from the five ACDC test cases of the worked example (the scan crops of Figures 1 and 2 and the values of the B20 table), it contains no image, mask or case-level data of the datasets, which must be obtained from their organizers. The accompanying article is in preparation. Research software, not for clinical use.

notes: Under the authors' direction, the large language model Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic) drafted the study protocol, wrote the code of all figures, and drew Figures 1, 2 and S1 through that code from a specification in which every label cites its source in the article. No image was generated or edited by a generative AI tool, and no reported number was computed by one: the scans are unmodified crops of ACDC test images, and every number is taken from the recorded outputs of the frozen pipeline and of the signed post-freeze analyses. The authors checked the numbers and citations against their sources and reviewed all code, text and figures. Cloud GPU training was supported by computing credits from Modal Labs, and the use of Claude by API credits from Anthropic's AI for Science program.
